elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 14(a): "This Agreement is governed in all respects by the laws of the State of New York without giving effect to its conflict of laws principles." Delaware was replaced with New York, an accepted preferred jurisdiction.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Rendered 14(a): "Each Party hereby irrevocably submits for all disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York." The competing mandate in Section 8 was conformed: "Any controversy or claim ... shall be resolved exclusively in the courts specified in Section 14(a)", removing the AAA arbitration mechanic. No alternate merits forum survives; the absence of a temporary-injunction carve-out does not defeat the element, which tolerates at most such a carve-out.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause selects "the laws of the State of New York", not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. This is intentional (the drafter targeted the preferred level), so the fallback level is simply not the level satisfied.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Forum is "the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York", which is not a Delaware, California, or London forum corresponding to a fallback governing law.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: New York law plus exclusive New York County state and federal court jurisdiction, with the conflicting mandatory AAA arbitration sentence in Section 8 replaced by a pointer to the Section 14(a) forum. Without that Section 8 edit the exclusive-merits-forum element would have been internally inconsistent, so the edit is required rather than extra.

Minimality holds: only the jurisdiction words (Delaware to New York), the venue words ("New York, New York" to "New York County, New York"), the arbitration mandate, and the now-inaccurate Section 8 heading were touched. The Customer-favourable jury waiver and the one-year limitation sentence in Section 8 were retained verbatim; no survival tails, procedures, or other boilerplate were added.

Intent preserved: the exclusivity, irrevocable submission, conflict-of-laws exclusion, and the surrounding Section 8 mechanics survive without contradiction, and the Section 8 pointer avoids a dangling or undefined forum.

Residual observation (not a defect requiring repair): Section 14(d) still refers to recovery of "arbitration" costs. It is conditional cost-recovery language, not an arbitration mandate, so it does not reopen a competing forum; if the counterparty raises it, a one-word conforming tidy could be offered, but leaving it is the more minimal choice.
